body: Navarathri 2026 runs October 11–20, and Bay Area temples mark all nine nights with special alankarams, poojas and cultural programs.

The Livermore Shiva-Vishnu Temple anchors the celebrations with a full ten-day Durga Pooja program: Mata Ki Chowki on Oct 16 (6–8 PM), Kanaka Durga Kumkumarchana (Oct 16, 6 PM), Saraswati Puja (Oct 16, 6:30 PM), the Bathukamma cultural celebration (Oct 18, 4 PM) and a Navaratri Garba night on Oct 25 (5–8 PM).
In Fremont, the Vedic Dharma Samaj temple hosts Devi Navarathri special poojas plus Garba evenings — arrive early, as parking fills fast during Navratri.
The Shiv Durga Temple in Santa Clara is a natural fit for the festival, with nine nights dedicated to Durga. The Sunnyvale Hindu Temple also runs special alankarams and poojas through the festival.
Practical tips: weekday evenings are less crowded than weekends; check each temple page here for the day's timings before you go, since festival schedules extend regular hours.

body: Every temple on this site is ranked by its approximate number of public Google reviews, observed in October 2026. The count is a rough proxy for how established and visited a temple is — not a verdict on spiritual merit.
Review counts change over time and differ across platforms, so each temple page shows the source and the observation date. Ratings are out of 5.

A small temple with 50 reviews and a 5.0 rating can be just as meaningful a visit as a 4,800-review landmark. Use the ranking to discover, the deity filters to narrow, and the festival calendar to plan.

body: Most Bay Area temples ask for modest dress — shoulders and knees covered. BAPS Milpitas is explicit about it and offers sarongs if needed.
Remove footwear before entering the sanctum; shoe racks are provided. Switch your phone to silent — and note that Livermore enforces a strict no-photography policy inside.
Prasadam is part of the experience: Livermore serves it free to all visitors, Sai Parivaar serves free prasadam on Thursdays, and the Sunnyvale temple's cafeteria serves lunch and dinner.
Festival days draw big crowds — arrive early, carpool where you can, and check the temple's website for any special schedule before heading out.
